cells.Title: Pruning preserves content needed by surviving states
cells.Requirement: Removing a snapshot shall preserve every content hash-and-length key required by any surviving indexed state, including content whose sole copy is in the removed snapshot. Preserved content shall not be repacked or recompressed. No index entry shall be added, removed or reordered; RelativePath, Length, LastWriteTimeStr, xxH2Hash, Duplicate and MediaMBPerSec shall remain unchanged. Only planned storage-location and stored-form fields may change, with each rewritten index receiving its own matching integrity evidence. A removal that endangers no content shall copy none.
cells.Rationale: Shared content can make an old snapshot hold the only copy needed by other states. Retention policy belongs to the backup host; safe removal and preservation belong to the backup system. Explicit surviving references prevent unreferenced copies and keep interrupted work checkable.
cells.AcceptanceCriteria: Removing the oldest, middle, newest or sole snapshot leaves every surviving state and the latest state byte-exact restorable, with raw and compressed content. Preserved bytes match their indexed hash and length; index changes are confined to planned storage-location and form fields with identical entry sets and valid integrity evidence. Safe removals copy zero bytes; a quiescent store holds each content key once.

cells.Title: Staging ownership and safe abandoned-run recovery
cells.Requirement: A backup shall establish exclusive staging ownership before using staging, keep its liveness observable throughout long blocking work, and abort without cleanup if ownership is lost. Diagnostic identity shall include the set, host, container, boot, process and start time; process identity alone shall not prove liveness across hosts or containers. Liveness updates shall occur every 60 seconds, verify the initial update synchronously, report later failures, never refresh a successor's ownership, and cease completely when stopped. A stale owner shall be declared dead only after its declared timeout, with a minimum of 1800 seconds, and unchanged liveness over a confirmation interval of max(90 seconds, declared heartbeat interval + 30 seconds), with the positive declared interval capped at 600 seconds. Unparseable records shall use the 1800-second and 90-second floors; unreadable evidence shall refuse. Future-dated evidence shall count as fresh. Fresh empty staging, live or changing ownership, prune ownership of any age, content-bearing staging, symbolic links and indeterminate access shall refuse; only stale empty or confirmed stale backup-marker-only staging may be reclaimed, subject to SR-083's incomplete-index exception. Recovery shall preserve unexpected content, recheck ownership after claiming abandoned staging, and retain it with guidance when safe cleanup or reversal fails. Concurrent reclaimers shall leave one owner; a former owner shall not alter or delete its successor's work. Ownership shall be checked before staging the prior index, preserving removed content, preserving superseded content, publishing the live index and finalizing the snapshot. Unreadable ownership evidence shall be retried up to three times about 300 ms apart; a changed identity shall abort immediately without cleanup. Final snapshots shall contain no active ownership record. Each branch shall log its distinct [SR-075/reclaimed], [SR-075/owner-live], [SR-075/content-refused], [SR-075/prune-held], [SR-075/lock-lost] or [SR-075/lock-held] token without adding exit codes. Exclusive mutation protection shall cover finalization even after marker removal; failure to acquire it shall refuse, while successful acquisition shall never substitute for abandoned-staging checks.
cells.Rationale: An interrupted run should not permanently block future backups, but an incorrect reclaim can destroy the only copy of saved content. Container process identities and clock offsets cannot establish safe ownership alone. Confirmed liveness, ownership checks and fail-closed cleanup protect against delayed or resumed writers, metadata caching and unexpected content. Longer stale thresholds delay recovery; shorter ones risk a live run. Distinct log outcomes let the backup host apply its own alarm policy.
cells.AcceptanceCriteria: A confirmed stale marker-only abandoned run is reclaimed with the reclaimed token and the next run completes; a live run is refused with owner identity, start time and last-liveness age and no store mutation. Liveness advances during a long blocking hash and update failures are reported. Content-bearing, prune-held, unreadable, linked or indeterminate staging remains untouched. Torn or unknown-schema records can recover only under the stated age and confirmation floors. Racing reclaimers leave one owner; a displaced owner aborts without touching successor state. Content appearing during recovery is preserved and guidance is shown. Changed ownership at any of the five protected boundaries aborts before that phase mutates the pool. A live owner with a slow clock is still refused. Final snapshots contain no active ownership metadata and prune without spurious unreferenced-content refusals. These outcomes hold on exFAT under Windows and Linux containers.

cells.Title: Measured compression decision
cells.Requirement: For newly written content with CompressEnabled=true, the system shall apply CompressProbe modes off|excluded-extensions|always, exact lowercase, default always. Disabled compression shall store raw without probing or resolving compression tooling. Mode off shall use the extension policy. Files below 256 KiB shall use that policy without probing in every mode; excluded-extensions shall exempt listed types. Otherwise a measured aggregate saving of at least 0.10 shall select compression, with no filename override. Missing measurements shall fall back to the extension policy with one WARN per written content group and shall not fail the run. Sampling shall not modify source or destination content, shall reject observed changes in source length or modification time, and shall cost no more than 3 × 256 KiB per newly written group. A readable duplicate shall serve measurement when the owner is locked; existing-content reuse and in-run twins shall not incur probes, and retrying group members shall not repeat the measurement. Each written group shall log one DEBUG compress-decision with reason and aggregate/window ratios, using Reason values CompressDisabled, ModeOff, BelowFloor, ListExempt, ProbeUnavailable, ProbeCompressible and ProbeIncompressible. Set summaries shall report Probe stored raw object/byte counts, Probe compressed object count and Probe reads byte count, with stored counts reflecting successful writes. Existing content shall not be re-formed; restore semantics, exit codes and ConfigVersion 2 shall remain unchanged. Stored extension and Compressed metadata shall agree with the actual decision.
cells.Rationale: Extensions alone cannot reveal compressibility, and a small compressible head must not send an otherwise incompressible large file through expensive compression. Aggregate measurement bounds that cost. Fallback preserves availability when sampling cannot run; shared group decisions bound reads and warnings. Sampling is deterministic within a host and run, though near-threshold results may vary across runtime versions; either stored form must remain byte-exact recoverable.
cells.AcceptanceCriteria: With compression disabled, every mode and extension class stores raw and performs no probe. Above 256 KiB under always, random bytes remain raw, text compresses, a random file with a 64 KiB text head remains raw, and one-third-text content compresses; listed archive or image extensions do not override measurements. Under off, the extension policy applies; excluded-extensions preserves exemptions and probes other eligible content; below the floor all modes use the extension policy. Files smaller than three sample windows use one full-file sample. Unreadable or vanished paths yield no measurement; a group with no readable member falls back with exactly one WARN without failing merely because of the probe. Random samples have aggregate ratio at least 0.98. Reused content and twins incur zero probe reads; retried groups probe once and warn at most once; a readable twin avoids ProbeUnavailable. Logs and summary counts match measured read cost and successfully stored objects, including reported container read bytes and elapsed cost. Invalid mode values fail with status 2 and no artifacts in JSON and CLIXML; absent mode resolves to always. Mixed-form output verifies clean and restores byte-exact through both restorers.

cells.Title: Exclusive store mutation through finalization
cells.Requirement: Backup, pruning, storage-form repair and kit refresh shall exclude concurrent participating store mutations for their whole operation, including direct API calls, state-dependent reads and snapshot finalization after active ownership metadata is removed. Pruning shall obtain exclusion before even completing previously committed deletion and retain it for the batch. Exclusion shall end after the operation or on failure and shall be released when its process dies. Dry-run mutation operations, read-only Verify, Snapshots, View and restores shall not obtain mutation exclusion. Windows exclusion shall apply among openers and SMB clients; Linux/macOS exclusion is limited to cooperating processes on the same kernel, including containers sharing storage, when the filesystem and runtime support locking. Cross-host SMB/NFS or mixed local/server access is not guaranteed there; older-owner liveness and confirmation safeguards remain required wherever exclusion is ineffective.
cells.Rationale: Finalization can temporarily lack ownership metadata while staging holds unique saved bytes. cells.Title: Conservative mutation-exclusion failure handling
cells.Requirement: Any inability to obtain mutation exclusion, including contention, access denial, transient external access, an invalid lock location or I/O failure, shall be treated as a live holder. After at most three attempts about 250 ms apart, the caller shall log [SR-075/lock-held] and refuse without creating, classifying, moving or deleting staging, data or indexes. Backup shall fail its set; named prune requests shall report Refused, staging-busy, code 2; repair and refresh shall throw and Verify shall report 2. A repair without a change root shall refuse likewise; a nonexistent change root shall be created before exclusion is obtained. cells.Title: Persistent mutation-exclusion infrastructure
cells.Requirement: Mutation-exclusion infrastructure shall remain usable when marked read-only and shall not be interpreted as user data, a snapshot or historical change content by any backup, audit, inventory, pruning or restore operation. Adding it shall not require refreshing existing restore kits.
cells.Rationale: Removing and recreating filesystem lock identity can let simultaneous processes hold different locks for the same store. Persistent empty infrastructure avoids that race and must remain invisible to content consumers.
cells.AcceptanceCriteria: After three runs the exclusion artifact remains empty; while held it does not change snapshot inventory, audit findings or byte-exact recovery of the latest and historical states. A read-only attribute does not prevent acquisition; Windows prevents deletion while held. Existing kits remain usable without refresh.
